prompt:
You are a scientific reflection agent for a coding-agent AI co-scientist.
Review type: simulation_review
Objective: Find the single appended system-prompt instruction that most improves a small headless coding agent's held-out-test pass rate on short self-contained Python implementation tasks whose prompts do not themselves instruct testing or verification. Hypotheses must be A/B-testable (baseline: no appended instruction; candidate: baseline plus exactly one instruction) and grounded in observed small-model failure modes: incomplete extraction of listed requirements, unverified edge cases, and premature completion. The agent under test already writes and runs its own ad-hoc tests when it chooses to; an intervention must add value beyond that default behavior.
Preferences: aligned with the research objective; plausible from code, benchmark, or literature evidence; novel or a novel combination of known techniques; testable with a concrete experiment; safe and auditable
Constraints: do not autonomously modify source code; do not claim measured improvement without benchmark evidence
Metrics: pass_rate; regression_count; tool_calls; wall_time; cost
Safety notes: human review required before applying code changes

Hypothesis:
- id: hyp-6744be5c7092
- title: Pre-Completion Spec Re-Read Instruction Raises Held-Out Pass Rate
- claim: Appending the instruction 'Before declaring the task done, re-read the complete task description and every docstring one final time, and for each stated behavior confirm your implementation handles it; fix anything that does not.' raises held-out pass rate versus a no-instruction baseline.
- rationale: Requirement omission is hypothesized to happen at read time: details absorbed early decay from working context by the time the agent finishes. A mandatory final re-read re-surfaces forgotten clauses exactly when the implementation exists to be checked against them, at much lower overhead than test-first or checklist scaffolds. It is the minimal intervention targeting the same failure mode, so it also serves as a dose-response comparison point for heavier scaffolds.
- assumptions: Omissions are recoverable at the end of a trial within remaining turn budget; The agent genuinely re-reads rather than pattern-matching a confirmation; Spec length fits comfortably in the agent's context at completion time
- risks: Late discovery of a missed requirement may exceed remaining budget to fix, converting omission into partial work with no pass-rate gain; Weakest-dose intervention may produce an effect too small to detect at the experiment's sample size; A perfunctory re-read yields no behavior change

Evidence:
- No evidence available.

Reason step by step through mechanism, intervention, expected measurements, each simulated outcome, and explicit failure conditions before deciding.
Return only valid JSON with:
decision, scores, strengths, weaknesses, safety_notes, findings, confidence, requires_revision, evidence_refs.
response: {"decision": "accept", "scores": {"alignment": 5, "plausibility": 3, "novelty": 2, "testability": 5, "safety": 5, "expected_impact": 3}, "strengths": ["Cheapest simulated timeline: one re-read turn plus targeted fixes; overhead never plausibly costs a trial", "Best case recovers exactly one forgotten clause per affected trial, which is enough on all-pass grading to flip a fail to a pass"], "weaknesses": ["Simulated same-reader-same-error path: the re-read repeats the original misparse and changes nothing \u2014 plausibly the modal path for never-encoded clauses", "Late-fix path can run out of turns on multi-clause misses, yielding partially-fixed fails indistinguishable from baseline fails in the primary metric"], "safety_notes": ["All simulated paths benign"], "findings": ["Keep as low-dose comparator; its simulated ceiling is the smallest of the family"], "confidence": 0.58, "requires_revision": false, "evidence_refs": []}
